qualification.reason: This is a Request for Quotes (RFQ) issued by the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance for the procurement of GPS hardware and software, including installation services, with a defined submission deadline, requirements, and award criteria.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR QUOTES
The New York State Department of Taxation and Finance (“DTF” or “Department”) has a need to monitor and manage a fleet of approximately ninety-three (93) vehicles.
Bids will not be considered unless the vendor submitting a bid meets the following minimum qualifications.
The award will be made to the responsive and responsible Bidder who provides the lowest overall cost and meets all requirements set forth in this RFQ.
Responses to this RFQ must be emailed to BFS.Contracts@tax.ny.gov no later than October 8, 2019 at 2:00 PM ET.

findings.title: Bidder must comply with MacBride Fair Employment Principles if operating in Northern Ireland
findings.fact: Contractor must either have no business operations in Northern Ireland or take lawful steps to conduct business in accordance with MacBride Fair Employment Principles and permit independent monitoring.

quotes.quote: In accordance with the MacBride Fair Employment Principles (Chapter 807 of the Laws of 1992), the Contractor hereby stipulates that the Contractor either (a) has no business operations in Northern Ireland, or (b) shall take lawful steps in good faith to conduct any business operations in Northern Ireland in accordance with the MacBride Fair Employment Principles (as described in Section 165 of the New York State Finance Law), and shall permit independent monitoring of compliance with such principles.

findings.title: Bidder must comply with equal employment opportunity requirements
findings.fact: Contractor must not discriminate and must undertake affirmative action to employ minority group members and women on State contracts.

quotes.quote: The Contractor will not discriminate against employees or applicants for employment because of race, creed, color, national origin, sex, age, disability or marital status, shall make and document its conscientious and active efforts to employ and utilize minority group members and women in its work force on State contracts and will undertake or continue existing programs of affirmative action to ensure that minority group members and women are afforded equal employment opportunities without discrimination.

findings.title: Bidder must comply with tropical hardwoods prohibition
findings.fact: Contractor must certify that all wood products comply with Section 165 of State Finance Law prohibiting tropical hardwoods unless exempted.

quotes.quote: The Contractor certifies and warrants that all wood products to be used under this contract award will be in accordance with, but not limited to, the specifications and provisions of Section 165 of the State Finance Law, (Use of Tropical Hardwoods) which prohibits purchase and use of tropical hardwoods, unless specifically exempted, by the State or any governmental agency or political subdivision or public benefit corporation.

findings.title: Bidder must comply with procurement lobbying restrictions
findings.fact: Offerer must affirm understanding and compliance with DTF procedures relating to permissible contacts during procurement as required by State Finance Law.

quotes.quote: Offerer affirms it has read, understands and agrees to comply with the guidelines of the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance relative to permissible contacts as required by the State Finance Law §§139-j(3) and 139-j(6)(b).

findings.title: Bidder must certify compliance with State Finance Law 139-k
findings.fact: Offerer must certify that all information provided to DTF with respect to State Finance Law 139-k is complete, true and accurate.

quotes.quote: I certify that all information provided to the DTF with respect to State Finance Law §139-k is complete, true and accurate.

findings.title: Department Responses to Bidder Questions Published
findings.fact: The Department will respond to bidder questions by September 30, 2019.

quotes.quote: Department Responses to Bidder Questions Published September 30, 2019

findings.title: Anticipated Notification of Intent to Award
findings.fact: The anticipated notification of intent to award is October 16, 2019.

quotes.quote: Anticipated Notification of Intent to Award October 16, 2019

findings.title: Issuance of Purchase Order
findings.fact: The purchase order is expected to be issued approximately 10 business days after notification of intent to award.

quotes.quote: Issuance of Purchase Order Approximately 10 business days after Notification of Intent to Award

findings.title: Tie Bid Determination
findings.fact: In the event of tie bids, the earliest bid received shall determine the winner.

quotes.quote: In the event tie bids are received by the Department, the earliest bid received shall determine the winner.

findings.title: Evaluation of Proposals
findings.fact: The Department reserves the right to evaluate, accept and/or reject any and all proposals, in whole or in part, and to waive technicalities, irregularities, and omissions if in the Department's judgment the best interests of the Department will be served.

quotes.quote: Evaluate, accept and/or reject any and all proposals, in whole or in part, and to waive technicalities, irregularities, and omissions if, in the Department’s judgment, the best interests of the Department will be served.

findings.title: Negotiation with Next Lowest Cost Responsible Bidder
findings.fact: The Department may conduct negotiations with the next lowest cost responsible Bidder should the Department be unsuccessful in negotiating an Agreement with the selected Bidder.

quotes.quote: Conduct negotiations with the next lowest cost responsible Bidder should the Department be unsuccessful in negotiating an Agreement with the selected Bidder.

findings.title: Future Installations
findings.fact: If future installations of hardware are required, DTF will pay for each installation according to the prices provided on Attachment 1 for the location in which the installation is needed.

quotes.quote: Although not anticipated, if future installations of hardware are required, DTF will pay for each installation according to the prices provided on Attachment 1 for the location in which the installation is needed.

findings.title: Records Retention and Access
findings.fact: Contractor must maintain complete and accurate records directly pertinent to contract performance for six years after the calendar year they were made, and must allow access to these records by the State Comptroller, Attorney General, and other authorized entities during normal business hours.

quotes.quote: The Contractor shall establish and maintain complete and accurate books, records, documents, accounts and other evidence directly pertinent to performance under this contract (hereinafter, collectively, "the Records"). The Records must be kept for the balance of the calendar year in which they were made and for six (6) additional years thereafter. The State Comptroller, the Attorney General and any other person or entity authorized to conduct an examination, as well as the agency or agencies involved in this contract, shall have access to the Records during normal business hours at an office of the Contractor within the State of New York or, if no such office is available, at a mutually agreeable and reasonable venue within the State, for the term specified above for the purposes of inspection, auditing and copying.

findings.title: Late Payment Governed by State Finance Law
findings.fact: Timeliness of payment and any interest for late payment will be governed by Article 11-A of the State Finance Law to the extent required by law.

quotes.quote: Timeliness of payment and any interest to be paid to Contractor for late payment shall be governed by Article 11-A of the State Finance Law to the extent required by law.

findings.title: No Arbitration for Disputes
findings.fact: Disputes involving the contract may not be submitted to binding arbitration (except where statutorily authorized) and must be heard in a court of competent jurisdiction of the State of New York.

quotes.quote: Disputes involving this contract, including the breach or alleged breach thereof, may not be submitted to binding arbitration (except where statutorily authorized), but must, instead, be heard in a court of competent jurisdiction of the State of New York.

findings.title: Procurement Lobbying Certification
findings.fact: By signing the agreement, the contractor certifies that all disclosures made under State Finance Law Sections 139-j and 139-k are complete, true, and accurate; intentionally false or incomplete certification may lead to termination.

quotes.quote: To the extent this agreement is a "procurement contract" as defined by State Finance Law Sections 139-j and 139-k, by signing this agreement the contractor certifies and affirms that all disclosures made in accordance with State Finance Law Sections 139-j and 139-k are complete, true and accurate. In the event such certification is found to be intentionally false or intentionally incomplete, the State may terminate the agreement by providing written notification to the Contractor in accordance with the terms of the agreement.

findings.title: Sales Tax Registration Certification
findings.fact: If the contract is defined by Tax Law Section 5-a, failure to make the required certification or a false certification is a material breach and may result in termination.

quotes.quote: To the extent this agreement is a contract as defined by Tax Law Section 5-a, if the contractor fails to make the certification required by Tax Law Section 5-a or if during the term of the contract, the Department of Taxation and Finance or the covered agency, as defined by Tax Law 5-a, discovers that the certification, made under penalty of perjury, is false, then such failure to file or false certification shall be a material breach of this contract and this contract may be terminated, by providing written notification to the Contractor in accordance with the terms of the agreement, if the covered agency determines that such action is in the best interest of the State.

findings.title: Minimum Qualifications for Bidders
findings.fact: Bidders must be the original manufacturer or authorized reseller of the hardware and software, and must be compliant with all applicable laws and regulations.
findings.business_implication: Only manufacturers or authorized resellers can bid, ensuring product authenticity and support. Non-compliance with laws could lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your company is an authorized reseller for the proposed GPS hardware and software, and ensure all legal and regulatory requirements are met before bidding.

quotes.quote: The Bidder must: • Be the original manufacturer or authorized reseller of the hardware and software to be provided; and • Be compliant with all applicable laws and regulations related to providing these services.

findings.title: New York State Vendor File Registration Required
findings.fact: Prior to award, the Bidder must be registered in the New York State Vendor File administered by the Office of the State Comptroller.
findings.business_implication: Without registration, the bidder cannot be awarded the contract, even if selected.
findings.action_recommendation: If not already registered, initiate the registration process with the New York State Vendor File immediately to ensure eligibility for award.

quotes.quote: Prior to being awarded an Agreement pursuant to this RFQ, the Bidder(s) must be registered in the New York State Vendor File (Vendor File) administered by the Office of the State Comptroller (OSC).

findings.title: Certification of Compliance with State Finance Law §139-k(5)
findings.fact: Bidders must complete and submit Attachment 4, Offerer Certification of Compliance with State Finance Law §139-k(5).
findings.business_implication: Failure to submit this certification may render the bid non-responsive and lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure Attachment 4 is completed accurately and included with the bid submission.

quotes.quote: Attachment 4, Offerer Certification of Compliance with State Finance Law §139-k(5) is to be completed and submitted with this bid.

findings.title: Bidder must not be from discriminatory jurisdiction
findings.fact: Bidders whose principal place of business is in a jurisdiction that penalizes New York State vendors may be denied contracts if goods/services are substantially produced/performed outside New York State.
findings.business_implication: Bidders from certain states (e.g., South Carolina, Alaska, West Virginia, Wyoming, Louisiana, Hawaii) may be ineligible if their goods/services are produced outside NY.
findings.action_recommendation: Check if your principal place of business is in a discriminatory jurisdiction and assess where the goods/services will be produced. If applicable, consider adjusting your bid strategy or seek legal advice.

quotes.quote: Bidders are hereby notified that if their principal place of business is located in a country, nation, province, state or political subdivision that penalizes New York State vendors, and if the goods or services they offer will be substantially produced or performed outside New York State, the Omnibus Procurement Act 1994 and 2000 amendments (Chapter 684 and Chapter 383, respectively) require that they be denied contracts which they would otherwise obtain.

findings.title: Deadline for Submission of Bidder Questions
findings.fact: The deadline for submission of bidder questions is September 25, 2019.
findings.business_implication: Missing this deadline means you cannot ask clarifying questions, potentially leading to misunderstandings or non-compliant bids.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit any questions regarding the RFQ before September 25, 2019, to ensure clarity and compliance.

quotes.quote: Deadline for Submission of Bidder Questions September 25, 2019

findings.title: Late Submissions May Not Be Accepted
findings.fact: Quotes received after the due date and time may not be accepted.
findings.business_implication: Missing the deadline could result in automatic disqualification, regardless of bid competitiveness.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure submission is completed well before the deadline (October 8, 2019, 2:00 PM ET) to avoid any last-minute issues.

quotes.quote: Quotes received after the due date and time may not be accepted.
Responses received by other methods or after the deadline may not be accepted.

findings.title: Date of Bid Submission Required
findings.fact: The Quote Response Form requires the bidder to provide the date of bid submission.
findings.business_implication: The date is used to determine the earliest bid in case of a tie, so accuracy is important.
findings.action_recommendation: Fill in the actual date of submission on the form to ensure compliance and avoid potential tie-breaker issues.

quotes.quote: Date of Bid Submission:

findings.title: Award Based on Lowest Overall Cost
findings.fact: The award will be made to the responsive and responsible Bidder who provides the lowest overall cost and meets all requirements set forth in this RFQ.
findings.business_implication: Price is the primary factor, but the bid must be fully compliant and responsive to be considered.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all requirements are met and provide the most competitive pricing to maximize chances of winning.

quotes.quote: The award will be made to the responsive and responsible Bidder who provides the lowest overall cost and meets all requirements set forth in this RFQ.

findings.title: Evaluation Criteria Not Specified in Provided Pages
findings.fact: The provided pages do not contain explicit evaluation criteria for the RFQ. The only mention of evaluation is in Attachment 1, which states that failure to answer clarifications may delay evaluation and result in disqualification.
findings.business_implication: The lack of detailed evaluation criteria may create uncertainty, but the emphasis is on responsiveness and completeness.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully complete all required forms and be prepared to respond promptly to any clarifications to avoid disqualification.

quotes.quote: The Department reserves the right to seek clarifications and ask questions based on the information provided on this form. Failure to answer all clarifications or questions may delay the evaluation of your bid and may result in a determination of non-responsiveness and disqualification of the bid.

findings.title: Term of Agreement
findings.fact: The Agreement will commence upon the issuance of a Purchase Order and shall be effective for a period of two (2) years.
findings.business_implication: The contract will be for a fixed two-year term, which affects pricing and resource commitment.
findings.action_recommendation: Factor the two-year term into pricing and ensure capacity to deliver over that period.

quotes.quote: The Agreement will commence upon the issuance of a Purchase Order and shall be effective for a period of two (2) years.
This Agreement will commence upon the issuance of a Purchase Order and shall be effective for a period of two (2) years.

findings.title: Price Guarantee
findings.fact: Prices as they appear on submitted bids must be guaranteed by the vendor for the term of the Agreement.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that the prices submitted are accurate and sustainable for the entire contract term, as they cannot be increased later. This may pose a risk if costs rise unexpectedly.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully calculate all costs, including potential future increases, and consider adding a contingency margin to the bid prices to mitigate the risk of cost overruns.

quotes.quote: Prices as they appear on submitted bids must be guaranteed by the vendor for the term of the Agreement.

findings.title: Payment Terms
findings.fact: Payment for invoices shall be rendered electronically unless paper check is expressly authorized by the Commissioner. Invoices cannot reflect charges in excess of the totals bid on Attachment 1 unless mutually agreed upon in writing.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to receive payments electronically and must strictly adhere to the bid pricing. Any additional costs must be pre-approved in writing, which may delay payment if not properly documented.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the company is set up for electronic payment with the State Comptroller's office. Maintain clear documentation of any agreed changes to pricing to avoid disputes.

quotes.quote: Payment for invoices submitted by the awarded Bidder shall only be rendered electronically unless payment by paper check is expressly authorized by the Commissioner, at the Commissioner’s sole discretion, due to extenuating circumstances.

Invoices cannot reflect charges in excess of the totals bid on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form, unless the additionally incurred costs are mutually agreed upon in writing between the Bidder and an authorized Department representative.

findings.title: Installation Costs
findings.fact: All installation costs must be provided on Attachment 1 and must be inclusive of all labor and travel. Charges for travel cannot be listed as separate line items.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must accurately estimate all installation-related expenses, including travel, and include them in the bid. Failure to do so could result in financial loss if actual costs exceed the bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly assess the installation requirements at all three locations and include a comprehensive cost estimate that covers all labor, travel, and any additional materials needed.

quotes.quote: All installation costs must be provided on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form, and must be inclusive of all labor and travel to the Department’s three (3) locations.
Charges for travel cannot be listed as separate line items on the bid response form. The prices bid for each item must be inclusive of all costs.

findings.title: No Cost Maintenance
findings.fact: If any devices require maintenance or replacement not resulting from negligence of DTF employees, the devices and/or services must be provided at no cost within 30 days of notification.
findings.business_implication: The bidder is obligated to provide free maintenance or replacement for any device issues not caused by the Department. This could lead to significant costs if many devices fail during the contract term.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the reliability of the proposed hardware and consider the potential costs of maintenance and replacement. Ensure that the bid price accounts for this risk, or negotiate a warranty that covers such costs.

quotes.quote: If any devices are identified by the Department to require maintenance or replacement, not resulting from the negligence of any DTF employee, the devices and/or services must be provided to the Department at no cost within 30 days of the Department’s notification.

findings.title: Set-Off Rights
findings.fact: The State has the right to withhold moneys due to the Contractor for set-off purposes, including amounts owed to the State under this or any other contract, tax delinquencies, and other monetary penalties.
findings.business_implication: The State can withhold payments to the bidder to cover any debts the bidder owes to the State, even if unrelated to this contract. This could impact cash flow and create financial risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the company has no outstanding debts or tax liabilities to the State of New York. Maintain good financial standing and monitor any potential set-off risks.

quotes.quote: The State shall have all of its common law, equitable and statutory rights of set-off. These rights shall include, but not be limited to, the State's option to withhold for the purposes of set-off any moneys due to the Contractor under this contract up to any amounts due and owing to the State with regard to this contract, any other contract with any State department or agency, including any contract for a term commencing prior to the term of this contract, plus any amounts due and owing to the State for any other reason including, without limitation, tax delinquencies, fee delinquencies or monetary penalties relative thereto.

findings.title: Contract Void Without Workers' Compensation Coverage
findings.fact: The contract shall be void and of no force and effect unless the Contractor provides and maintains workers' compensation coverage during the life of the contract.
findings.business_implication: Failure to maintain workers' compensation coverage will render the contract void, meaning the contractor will not be entitled to payment and may face legal consequences. This is a critical compliance requirement.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that workers' compensation insurance is in place and maintained for the entire duration of the contract. Provide proof of coverage to the State as required and monitor renewal dates to avoid lapses.

quotes.quote: In accordance with Section 142 of the State Finance Law, this contract shall be void and of no force and effect unless the Contractor shall provide and maintain coverage during the life of this contract for the benefit of such employees as are required to be covered by the provisions of the Workers' Compensation Law.

findings.title: Contractor Consents to Service of Process by Mail
findings.fact: Contractor consents to service of process by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested.
findings.business_implication: The contractor agrees to accept legal documents via mail, which may affect how legal notices are delivered and could impact response times.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the organization has a reliable process for receiving and handling certified mail to avoid missing legal notices. Designate a responsible person to monitor such deliveries.

quotes.quote: In addition to the methods of service allowed by the State Civil Practice Law & Rules ("CPLR"), Contractor hereby consents to service of process upon it by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested.

findings.title: Termination for False Certification Under Procurement Lobbying Law
findings.fact: The State may terminate the agreement if the contractor's certification under State Finance Law Sections 139-j and 139-k is found to be intentionally false or incomplete.
findings.business_implication: Providing false or incomplete information regarding procurement lobbying activities can lead to termination of the contract, which could result in financial losses and reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all disclosures and certifications related to procurement lobbying are accurate and complete. Implement internal controls to verify the truthfulness of information before submission.

quotes.quote: In the event such certification is found to be intentionally false or intentionally incomplete, the State may terminate the agreement by providing written notification to the Contractor in accordance with the terms of the agreement.

findings.title: Termination for False Tax Certification
findings.fact: If the contractor fails to make the certification required by Tax Law Section 5-a or if the certification is false, the contract may be terminated.
findings.business_implication: Failure to provide a true tax certification or providing a false one is considered a material breach, allowing the State to terminate the contract, which could lead to loss of revenue and legal penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that the organization is registered to collect sales and compensating use tax as required, and ensure the certification is accurate. Maintain compliance with tax laws throughout the contract term.

quotes.quote: if the contractor fails to make the certification required by Tax Law Section 5-a or if during the term of the contract, the Department of Taxation and Finance or the covered agency, as defined by Tax Law 5-a, discovers that the certification, made under penalty of perjury, is false, then such failure to file or false certification shall be a material breach of this contract and this contract may be terminated, by providing written notification to the Contractor in accordance with the terms of the agreement, if the covered agency determines that such action is in the best interest of the State.

findings.title: Contractor Must Comply with Information Security Breach Notification Act
findings.fact: Contractor shall comply with the New York State Information Security Breach and Notification Act.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must have procedures in place to detect, respond to, and notify affected parties in the event of a data breach, as required by New York law. Non-compliance could result in penalties and damage to reputation.
findings.action_recommendation: Review and update data security policies to align with the NYS Information Security Breach and Notification Act. Ensure that incident response plans include timely notification to the State and affected individuals as required.

quotes.quote: Contractor shall comply with the provisions of the New York State Information Security Breach and Notification Act (General Business Law Section 899-aa; State Technology Law Section 208).

findings.title: Termination for Unacceptable Replacement Devices
findings.fact: The Department reserves the right to terminate the Agreement if replacement devices are deemed unacceptable.
findings.business_implication: The Department has broad discretion to reject replacement devices and terminate the contract, which could lead to loss of revenue and potential liability for the bidder if replacements are not accepted.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that replacement devices meet or exceed the specifications and are compatible with the Department's requirements. Maintain clear communication with the Department regarding any replacements and seek written approval before proceeding.

quotes.quote: The Department reserves the right to terminate the Agreement if such replacement devices are deemed unacceptable.

findings.title: Termination for False Certification
findings.fact: DTF reserves the right to terminate the Agreement if the certification filed by the Offerer/bidder was intentionally false or intentionally incomplete.
findings.business_implication: Providing false or incomplete certification can lead to immediate termination, which would result in loss of the contract and potential legal consequences.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all certifications and disclosures are accurate and complete. Implement internal review processes to verify the truthfulness of all submitted information before signing.

quotes.quote: DTF reserves the right to terminate this Agreement in the event it is found that the certification filed by the Offerer/bidder in accordance with New York State Finance Law §139-k was intentionally false or intentionally incomplete.

findings.title: Termination for Non-Discrimination Violations
findings.fact: Contractor is subject to possible termination of the contract and forfeiture of all moneys due for a second or subsequent violation of non-discrimination provisions.
findings.business_implication: Violations of non-discrimination provisions can lead to fines and, for repeat violations, termination and loss of all payments, which could be financially devastating.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust equal employment opportunity policies and training to ensure compliance with all non-discrimination laws. Monitor subcontractors and employees to prevent violations.

quotes.quote: Contractor is subject to fines of $50.00 per person per day for any violation of Section 220-e or Section 239 as well as possible termination of this contract and forfeiture of all moneys due hereunder for a second or subsequent violation.

findings.title: Termination for Violation of Iran Divestment Act
findings.fact: If the contractor violates the Iran Divestment Act certification, the state agency may declare the contractor in default, which could lead to termination.
findings.business_implication: Violating the Iran Divestment Act can result in being declared in default, leading to termination and potential sanctions, which would harm the company's reputation and financial standing.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct thorough due diligence to ensure compliance with the Iran Divestment Act. Regularly check the Prohibited Entities List and ensure no subcontractors are on it. If a violation is alleged, respond promptly and cease any prohibited activities within 90 days.

quotes.quote: If the person fails to demonstrate that it has ceased its engagement in the investment activity which is in violation of the Act within 90 days after the determination of such violation, then the state agency shall take such action as may be appropriate and provided for by law, rule, or contract, including, but not limited to, imposing sanctions, seeking compliance, recovering damages, or declaring the Contractor in default.

findings.title: Ambiguity in Data Reliability Determination
findings.fact: The RFQ requires that the GPS devices must have the ability to continuously log vehicle data, regardless of any outages in network coverage, resulting in no missing data, and that this data must be deemed reliable by the Department. However, it also states that the Department reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to make the final determination of whether the proposed solution includes information that is deemed reliable, creating ambiguity about the standard for data reliability.
findings.business_implication: The Department's sole discretion to determine data reliability introduces uncertainty, as the bidder may meet technical requirements but still be deemed non-compliant if the Department is not satisfied, potentially leading to disputes or termination.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify the reliability criteria with the Department before bidding. Ensure the proposed solution includes robust data logging and redundancy features. Document all technical capabilities and seek written confirmation of acceptance criteria.

quotes.quote: Have the ability to continuously log vehicle data, regardless of any outages in network coverage, resulting in no missing data. This data must be deemed reliable by the Department.
The Department reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to make the final determination of whether the proposed solution includes information that is deemed reliable.
